title: Mrs. Doubtfire
tagline: Nanny's cooking tonight. Mind the frosting.
about: A divorced dad disguises himself as an elderly British nanny to spend time with his kids.
cue: Serve dessert when Daniel's face ends up in the frosting.

    StartersRestaurant garlic prawnsPrawns tossed in garlic and chilli butter with stock and lemonHow to make it80g butter6 garlic cloves1 pinch chilli flakes600g green prawns60ml chicken stock1 lemon1 bunch parsley1 crusty loafPeel the prawns and slice the garlic.Melt the butter until foaming, add the garlic and chilli and cook briefly.Add the prawns and toss over high heat until just pink.Add the stock and lemon juice and bubble briefly. Finish with chopped parsley and serve with crusty bread.Euphegenia's tea sandwichesEgg and cress, and dill cream cheese with cucumber, crusts off, cut in fingersHow to make it4 eggs2 tbsp mayonnaise1 bunch watercress150g cream cheese1 bunch dill1 Lebanese cucumber12 slices of white breadBoil the eggs hard, cool and peel.Mash the eggs with the mayonnaise and chopped watercress. Mix the cream cheese with dill.Spread the bread with the cream cheese, layer with egg and thin cucumber, and close up.Cut off the crusts and cut into fingers.San Francisco sourdough burrata bitesThe Hillard family home in San FranciscoHow to make itAs written, serves 4Garlic-rubbed sourdough toasts topped with torn burrata, balsamic cherry tomatoes and basil, a crack of pepper and a drizzle of good olive oil.Slice 1 sourdough baguette into 16 pieces, brush with oil and grill or toast until golden, then rub with a cut garlic clove.Halve 250g cherry tomatoes and toss with 1 tbsp balsamic, olive oil and salt.Tear 2 burrata over the toasts, spoon on the tomatoes and finish with basil, pepper and a drizzle of oil.MainsShepherd's pie she passes off as hersLamb and carrot pie in Worcestershire gravy under baked buttery mashHow to make it750g lamb mince1 brown onion2 carrots2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce250ml water1kg potatoes60g butter100ml full cream milkDice the onion and carrots. Peel and chop the potatoes.Brown the mince, add the onion and carrot, then the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and water. Simmer.Boil the potatoes and mash with the butter and milk.Top the mince with the mash and bake at 200°C until golden.Miranda's birthday steak, no cayenneMiranda's birthday dinner, the night of the cayenne pepperHow to make itAs written, serves 4Sirloin seared hard and basted with butter and thyme, sliced over crispy potatoes with a peppercorn sauce, spice kept well off the plate.Salt 4 sirloin steaks the night before.Roast 1kg diced potatoes in oil at 220°C for 40 minutes.Sear the steaks in a smoking pan for 3 minutes a side, add 40g butter and thyme and baste for 1 minute, then rest 5 minutes.In the pan cook 1 shallot with 1 tbsp crushed peppercorns, add 150ml beef stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick.SweetsFrosting face cakeSponge layers with mascarpone cream, piled high with fresh strawberriesHow to make it200g butter230g caster sugar4 eggs200g self-raising flour250g mascarpone300ml thickened cream500g strawberriesBeat the butter with most of the sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour.Bake in two tins at 175°C.Cool the cakes.Whip the mascarpone with the cream and remaining sugar.Fill and cover the cake, then pile on halved strawberries.DrinksA proper cuppaBlack tea brewed in a warmed pot, milk and sugar on the sideHow to make it4 tea bags of English breakfast tea1 L boiling water200ml full cream milkcaster sugar, to serveWarm the teapot with hot water and tip it out.Add the tea bags and freshly boiled water and brew.Pour into four cups with milk, and sugar on the side.
